## Exploratory Data Analysis 

We load the required data: Mexico City Population and Manzana level polygons. 

```{r}
### Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------

df_censo <- read_csv(file=paste0(RAW_DATA,CENSO_FOLDER, CENSO_FILE) )
df_mznas  <- st_read(paste0(RAW_DATA, MARCOGEO_FOLDER, MARCO_FILE), quiet = TRUE)


```



```{r}
### Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data TRransformations and filters 

# Create CVEGEO for census
df_censo <- df_censo |> 
  mutate(
    CVEGEO = paste0(ENTIDAD,MUN,LOC,AGEB,MZA)
  ) 

# Left Join 
df <- df_mznas |> left_join(
  df_censo , by = "CVEGEO"
) 

# Filter just the data that interest us 
df <- df |>
      # Just CDMX 
      filter(CVE_ENT == '09') |>
      # Non -aggregated values 
      filter(MZA != '00') |>
      # Censured Data
      filter(POBMAS != '*' & POBFEM != '*') |>
      filter(POBMAS != '0' & POBFEM != '0') |>
      filter(P_60YMAS != '*') |>
      filter(P_60YMAS != '0') |>
      # Select columns of interest
      select(CVEGEO, MZA, POBTOT, POBFEM, POBMAS,P_60YMAS)  |>
      # Variable Transformations 
      mutate(
        POBMAS = as.numeric(POBMAS),
        POBFEM = as.numeric(POBFEM),
        P_60YMAS = as.numeric(P_60YMAS),
        WpM_rate = POBFEM/POBMAS,
        W_per = POBFEM/POBTOT
      )
    


head(df)

```
```{r}

pal <- colorNumeric(
  palette = c("white", "darkblue"),   # use a color vector or palette name
  domain = df$P_60YMAS
)

leaflet(df |> st_transform(4326)) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addPolygons(
    color = "transparent",
    weight = 1,
    fillColor = ~pal(P_60YMAS),
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    label = ~paste0("POBTOT: ", P_60YMAS),
    group = "Total Pob"
  )

```


Poblation Pyramid 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# df: your data.frame (one row per geography). Filter if needed.
df1 <- df_censo |> slice(1)

# Cleanning 
pop_cols <- c(
  "POBTOT", "POBFEM", "POBMAS",
  "P_0A2_F","P_0A2_M",
  "P_3A5_F","P_3A5_M",
  "P_6A11_F","P_6A11_M",
  "P_12A14_F","P_12A14_M",
  "P_15A17_F","P_15A17_M",
  "P_18A24_F","P_18A24_M",
  "P_60YMAS_F","P_60YMAS_M"
)

df1 <- df1 |>
  mutate(across(all_of(pop_cols), ~ as.numeric(str_replace_all(as.character(.), "\\*", "0"))))


# Infering range 25-59 from data
df1 <- df1 |>
  mutate(
    P_25A59_F = pmax(
      0,
      POBFEM - (P_0A2_F + P_3A5_F + P_6A11_F + P_12A14_F + P_15A17_F + P_18A24_F + P_60YMAS_F)
    ),
    P_25A59_M = pmax(
      0,
      POBMAS - (P_0A2_M + P_3A5_M + P_6A11_M + P_12A14_M + P_15A17_M + P_18A24_M + P_60YMAS_M)
    )
  )

# Pyramid Data

age_bins <- c("P_0A2","P_3A5","P_6A11","P_12A14","P_15A17","P_18A24","P_25A59","P_60YMAS")
cols_keep <- c(paste0(age_bins, "_F"), paste0(age_bins, "_M"))

pyr <- df1 |>
  select(all_of(c("POBTOT", cols_keep))) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(cols_keep), names_to = "var", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(
    sex = if_else(str_ends(var, "_F"), "Feminine", "Masculine"),
    age = str_remove(var, "_[FM]$"),
    age = factor(age, levels = age_bins),
    n = as.numeric(n)
  )

# Plot as % of total
pyr <- pyr |>
  mutate(
    value = 100 * n / POBTOT,
    y = if_else(sex == "Feminine", -value, value),
    label = sprintf("%.1f%%", value)
  )

age_labels <- c(
  P_0A2 = "0–2",
  P_3A5 = "3–5",
  P_6A11 = "6–11",
  P_12A14 = "12–14",
  P_15A17 = "15–17",
  P_18A24 = "18–24",
  P_25A59 = "25–59",
  P_60YMAS = "60+"
)

# Plot
ggplot(pyr, aes(x = age, y = y, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = age_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "%"),
    breaks = pretty_breaks(6)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Age group",
    y = "% of total population",
    fill = NULL,
    title = "Population pyramid"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


```
